request.input:
You repair a Boolean network model of the DNA damage response (a published model, Gupta et al. 2023).
A claim read from the literature was turned into a rule change by a fixed template, and an exact solver rejected the
change: the edited network contradicts behaviours the model must keep (the verification cases). Propose another rule
for the node that still expresses the claim but passes those cases.

Rules are written with node names and the operators ! (not), & (and), | (or) and parentheses. A node is 1 when active.
DNA_damage is the only input. These are the nodes you may use: AKT, AMPK_MAPK, ATM_pH2AX, ATR, BAX, BCL2, CHK1, CHK2, Caspase, Cdc25, Cdc2_CycB, DNA_PK, DNA_damage, E2F1, Mdm2, Myc, PTEN, PUMA, RB, Sirt1, TUG1, ULK1_Beclin1, WWP1, Wee1, Wip1, hTERT, mTORC1, mTORC2, miR221, p21, p53, p53_A, p53_INP1, p53_K

CLAIM: CHK1 activates p53   (2 paper(s))
EVIDENCE:
- PMC3819289 (review statement about DNA damage response): "DNA damage response is initiated with the formation of foci consisting of γ-H2AX, 53BP1, NBS1, and MDC1, and leads to activation of ATM/ATR and Chk1/Chk2, which in turn phosphorylate and stabilize p53 [18]."
- PMC3913755 (review statement citing prior work): "p53 could also be activated by Chk1/Chk2 at Ser-20."

NODE TO CHANGE: p53
CURRENT RULE:   p53, (ATM_pH2AX | (!Mdm2 & AMPK_MAPK & !hTERT)) | CHK2
TEMPLATE RULE (rejected): p53, ((ATM_pH2AX | (!Mdm2 & AMPK_MAPK & !hTERT)) | CHK2) | CHK1

WHY IT WAS REJECTED (counterexamples from the solver; "setting" fixes nodes to 0 or 1, a phenotype is read from the
fixed points; the witness is a fixed point of the edited network):
- V04 (Figure 3, TUG1 KO); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'TUG1': 0}: unexpected; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis'] (exact), found ['apoptosis', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 0, 'AMPK_MAPK': 0, 'Mdm2': 0, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'hTERT': 0, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'mTORC1': 1, 'mTORC2': 1, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0, 'CHK2': 0, 'CHK1': 1}
- V05 (Figure 3, miR-221 E1); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'miR221': 1}: unexpected; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis'] (exact), found ['apoptosis', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 0, 'AMPK_MAPK': 0, 'Mdm2': 0, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'hTERT': 0, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'mTORC1': 1, 'mTORC2': 1, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0, 'CHK2': 0, 'CHK1': 1}
- V06 (Figure 3, miR-221 E1 + TUG1 KO); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'miR221': 1, 'TUG1': 0}: unexpected; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis'] (exact), found ['apoptosis', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 0, 'AMPK_MAPK': 0, 'Mdm2': 0, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'hTERT': 0, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'mTORC1': 1, 'mTORC2': 1, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0, 'CHK2': 0, 'CHK1': 1}

Requirements, all checked by the solver afterwards:
- CHK1 must be able to switch p53 on and never off: it acts on p53 only in the direction 'activates'.
- Keep every influence the current rule has: every node in the current rule must still affect the new rule in the same way.
- Use only the nodes listed above. Do not use p53 in its own rule.
- You may restrict WHEN the claimed effect applies by combining it with other nodes, if the evidence context (cell
  type, condition) or the counterexample suggests a condition. Say which condition you chose and why. Do not invent a
  mechanism the evidence does not support.
- If no rule can both express the claim and pass the cases, set give_up to true and explain.

Answer as JSON: {"rule": "<expression only, no node name and no comma>", "explanation": "...", "give_up": false}.

text: {"explanation": "Restricted CHK1 effect to AMPK_MAPK-positive contexts: (CHK1 & AMPK_MAPK). Witnesses V04-V06 all have ATM_pH2AX=0, AMPK_MAPK=0, CHK2=0 with CHK1=1 driving spurious p53=1 -> senescence. Requiring AMPK_MAPK blocks this de-novo route. ATM_pH2AX or CHK2 gating would make CHK1 redundant since they already OR-activate p53 in current rule, violating the activates requirement, while AMPK gating preserves a non-redundant CHK1 influence and only enhances the existing stress-kinase arm. This reflects the evidence context of co-activation of ATM/ATR and Chk1/Chk2 in DDR, without claiming a new molecular mechanism.", "give_up": false, "rule": "ATM_pH2AX | (!Mdm2 & AMPK_MAPK & !hTERT) | CHK2 | (CHK1 & AMPK_MAPK)"}
